votes.refutation: The finding rests on a false premise: GitHub does allow submitting an APPROVE review on a draft pull request. Draft status only blocks merging (and suppresses automatic CODEOWNERS review requests); the reviews endpoint accepts `event: APPROVE` on drafts, and the GitHub UI offers "Approve" on draft PRs. The only 422 the reviews endpoint returns for APPROVE is "Can not approve your own pull request", which does not apply to a GitHub App reviewing a bot-authored PR. Because the approval is pinned to the reviewed head via `commit_id`, it remains valid when the PR flips to ready, which is exactly the contract documented at review_pr.py:587-589 and tasks.py:162-164 and asserted by the end-to-end test at test_integration.py:1385-1425. There is therefore no "approval step fails for every self-driving draft PR" scenario and no retry loop; the draft carve-out is deliberate, narrowly scoped (test_review_pr.py:590-594), and already tested. The finding's own suggestion ("verify the GitHub review API behavior for drafts") resolves against it once verified. Not a defect.
